seed.note: Live coding, sometimes referred to as on-the-fly programming, is a performing art form and creativity technique where source code is written in an improvised way, often for creating music, imagery, and light art; sometimes combining improvised dance, poetry, and kinds of performance outside the code itself. It is particularly prevalent in computer music, combining elements of human and algorithmic composition.

crossover.title: Earworms
crossover.body: An earworm or brainworm, also described as sticky music or stuck song syndrome, is a catchy or memorable piece of music or saying that continuously occupies a person's mind even after it is no longer being played or spoken about. Involuntary Musical Imagery (INMI) is most common after earworms, but INMI as a label is not solely restricted to earworms; musical hallucinations also fall into this category, although they are not the same thing. Earworms are considered to be a common type of involuntary cognition. Some of the phrases often used to describe earworms include "musical imagery repetition" and "involuntary musical imagery".

items.title: MTHRBORD releases ACL2500, a FREE API 2500-style bus compressor
items.take: MTHRBORD.STUDIO has released ACL2500, a free stereo VCA bus compressor for macOS and Windows, modeled from measurements and recordings of a real API 2500. The developer measured how the hardware responds across different threshold, ratio, attack, release, and knee settings.

items.title: Eventide SplitEQ 2 Review: Does It Live Up To Its Claims?
items.take: Five years ago, Eventide’s SplitEQ was unique for its ability to separate and sculpt the transient and tonal parts of a sound.
